source.text: וּבָעֵ֣ת הַהִיא֩ יַעֲמֹ֨ד מִֽיכָאֵ֜ל הַשַּׂ֣ר הַגָּד֗וֹל הָעֹמֵד֮ עַל־בְּנֵ֣י עַמֶּךָ֒ וְהָיְתָה֙ עֵ֣ת צָרָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֤ר לֹֽא־נִהְיְתָה֙ מִֽהְי֣וֹת גּ֔וֹי עַ֖ד הָעֵ֣ת הַהִ֑יא וּבָעֵ֤ת הַהִיא֙ יִמָּלֵ֣ט עַמְּךָ֔ כָּל־הַנִּמְצָ֖א כָּת֥וּב בַּסֵּֽפֶר׃

records.literal_gloss: And at the time that will arise Michael, the prince the great, who stands over [the] sons of your people; and there will be a time of distress such as not has been since there was a nation until the time that; and at the time that will escape your people, everyone who is found written in the book.

en.L: "At that time Michael will arise, the great prince who stands over the sons of your people. And there will be a time of distress such as has not been since there was a nation until that time. But at that time your people will escape, everyone who is found written in the book.
en.B: "At that time Michael, the great prince who protects your people, will arise. There will be a time of distress such as has not happened from the beginning of the nations until then. But at that time your people will be rescued, everyone whose name is found written in the book.
en.R: "At that time Michael will come. He is the powerful ruling angel who protects your people. There will be a time of terrible trouble, worse than any time since nations first began. But at that time your people will be saved, everyone whose name is written in God's book.

fr.L: En ce temps-là se lèvera Michel, le grand prince, qui se tient pour les fils de ton peuple. Et ce sera un temps de détresse tel qu’il n’y en a pas eu depuis qu’il existe une nation jusqu’à ce temps-là. Mais en ce temps-là ton peuple échappera, quiconque sera trouvé inscrit dans le livre.
fr.B: En ce temps-là se lèvera Michel, le grand prince qui protège ton peuple. Ce sera un temps de détresse comme il n’y en a jamais eu depuis que les nations existent jusqu’à ce jour-là. Mais en ce temps-là ton peuple sera délivré, tous ceux dont le nom se trouvera inscrit dans le livre.
fr.R: En ce temps-là, Michel viendra. C’est le puissant ange qui gouverne et qui protège ton peuple. Ce sera un temps de terrible détresse, pire que tout ce qui est arrivé depuis que les nations existent. Mais en ce temps-là, ton peuple sera sauvé, tous ceux dont le nom est écrit dans le livre de Dieu.

decisions.choice: at that time: the time of the end of 11:40-45
decisions.reason: The messenger's speech goes on without a break from chapter 11. "That time" is the time of the end (11:40), when the king comes to his end (11:45). The chapter division is not in the Hebrew text.

decisions.choice: Michael will arise, who stands over your people: he rises to act for them
decisions.reason: "Arise" and "stand" may mean that Michael rises to defend his people, as he fought for them in 10:13, 21, or that he takes his stand in the heavenly court. Revelation 12:7 pictures Michael and his angels at war with the dragon.

decisions.choice: a time of distress such as has never been: Matthew 24:21
decisions.reason: Jesus takes up these words for the great distress before the end: "such as has not happened from the beginning of the world until now, nor ever will" (Matthew 24:21; Mark 13:19). Jeremiah 30:7 speaks of a day like no other, "a time of distress for Jacob", yet he will be saved out of it.

decisions.choice: written in the book: the list of those who belong to God
decisions.reason: God keeps a book of the living, or of his people (Exodus 32:32-33; Psalm 69:29; Malachi 3:16). Those whose names are in it are rescued. Compare Philippians 4:3 and Revelation 20:12, 15.

decisions.choice: the great prince (L, B); the powerful ruling angel (R)
decisions.reason: The table for Daniel gives "prince" at Literal and Balanced and "ruling angel" at Readable for sar used of an angel (see 10:13). Every level opens with a quotation mark, since the messenger's speech goes on in a new paragraph.

decisions.choice: God's book (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says whose book it is (m4).

decisions.choice: "un temps de détresse" at every level (R "un temps de terrible détresse")
decisions.reason: The term sheet keeps the words of the published Matthew 24:21, to which the meaning decision points, so a reader can see the echo.

source.text: וְרַבִּ֕ים מִיְּשֵׁנֵ֥י אַדְמַת־עָפָ֖ר יָקִ֑יצוּ אֵ֚לֶּה לְחַיֵּ֣י עוֹלָ֔ם וְאֵ֥לֶּה לַחֲרָפ֖וֹת לְדִרְא֥וֹן עוֹלָֽם׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And many of [the] sleepers of [the] ground of dust will awake, these to life of perpetuity, and these to reproaches, to abhorrence of perpetuity.

en.L: And many of those who sleep in the ground of dust will awake, some to everlasting life, and some to reproaches, to everlasting abhorrence.
en.B: Many who sleep in the dust of the earth will awake, these to everlasting life, and those to shame and everlasting contempt.
en.R: Many who have died will rise to life again. Some will rise to life that lasts forever. Others will rise to shame and disgrace that last forever.

fr.L: Et beaucoup de ceux qui dorment dans la terre de poussière se réveilleront, les uns pour la vie éternelle, et les autres pour les opprobres, pour l’horreur éternelle.
fr.B: Beaucoup de ceux qui dorment dans la poussière de la terre se réveilleront, les uns pour la vie éternelle, les autres pour la honte et pour un mépris éternel.
fr.R: Beaucoup de ceux qui sont morts reviendront à la vie. Certains revivront pour une vie qui dure toujours. D’autres revivront pour connaître la honte et le déshonneur pour toujours.

decisions.choice: those who sleep in the dust of the earth will awake: the dead will rise
decisions.reason: Sleep is a picture of death (Psalm 13:4; Job 14:12; Jeremiah 51:39), and the dust is the grave (Genesis 3:19; Job 7:21). To awake from that sleep is to be raised from death. Isaiah 26:19 has the same picture: "Awake and shout for joy, dwellers in the dust!" This verse is the clearest promise in the Old Testament of the raising of the dead to judgment.

decisions.choice: many will awake, some to everlasting life and some to everlasting contempt
decisions.reason: "Many" may mean that not all the dead are raised here, but those of the time of distress (the faithful who died, and their persecutors); or it may mean "the many", that is, all, as in Isaiah 53:11-12. The text speaks of two outcomes and does not say more. Jesus takes up the picture in John 5:28-29: all who are in the tombs will hear his voice and come out, those who did good to the resurrection of life, those who did evil to the resurrection of judgment.

decisions.choice: everlasting abhorrence: lasting disgust
decisions.reason: The word for "abhorrence" is found elsewhere only in Isaiah 66:24, of the bodies of the rebels against God, "an abhorrence to all flesh". The wicked are raised to lasting shame.

decisions.choice: those who sleep in the dust of the earth will awake (L, B); many who have died will rise to life again (R); everlasting life (L, B); life that lasts forever (R)
decisions.reason: The wording follows the terms note for Daniel: Literal and Balanced keep the image of sleep and waking, and Readable says what it means (m1). "Everlasting life" follows the table, with "life that lasts forever" at Readable. Literal says "the ground of dust" as the Hebrew has it.

decisions.choice: shame and everlasting contempt (B); shame and disgrace that last forever (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "reproaches" and "abhorrence", the word used in Isaiah 66:24 at Literal; Balanced and Readable use common words.

decisions.choice: "la vie éternelle" (L, B), "une vie qui dure toujours" (R); "ceux qui dorment dans la poussière ... se réveilleront" kept at Literal and Balanced
decisions.reason: As the term sheet sets, with the published John 5:29's "la vie" for the echo; Readable says plainly that the dead will rise, as the English Readable does.

source.text: וְהַ֨מַּשְׂכִּלִ֔ים יַזְהִ֖רוּ כְּזֹ֣הַר הָרָקִ֑יעַ וּמַצְדִּיקֵי֙ הָֽרַבִּ֔ים כַּכּוֹכָבִ֖ים לְעוֹלָ֥ם וָעֶֽד׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And those having insight will shine like [the] brightness of the vault, and those making righteous the many, like the stars, forever and ever.

en.L: "And those who have insight will shine like the brightness of the vault [of heaven], and those who turn the many to righteousness, like the stars forever and ever.
en.B: "Those who are wise will shine like the brightness of the sky, and those who lead many to righteousness, like the stars forever and ever.
en.R: "The wise leaders will shine as brightly as the sky. Those who have led many people to do what is right will shine like the stars forever and ever.

fr.L: Et ceux qui ont du discernement brilleront comme l’éclat de la voûte [céleste], et ceux qui amènent la multitude à la justice, comme les étoiles, à toujours et à jamais.
fr.B: Les sages brilleront comme l’éclat du ciel, et ceux qui conduisent beaucoup de gens à la justice brilleront comme les étoiles, pour toujours et à jamais.
fr.R: Les sages qui guident le peuple brilleront autant que le ciel. Ceux qui ont aidé beaucoup de gens à faire ce qui est juste brilleront comme les étoiles, pour toujours.

decisions.choice: those who turn the many to righteousness: Isaiah 53:11
decisions.reason: The words echo the servant of the LORD, who "will make many righteous" (Isaiah 53:11) and who "will act wisely" (Isaiah 52:13), the verb from which "those who have insight" comes. The wise teachers of 11:33-35, some of whom died, are given the servant's reward.

decisions.choice: the brightness of the vault: the shining sky
decisions.reason: The word is the one for the vault of the sky in Genesis 1:6-8 and the gleaming expanse of Ezekiel 1:22. The wise will shine like the sky itself.

decisions.choice: they will shine like the stars: Matthew 13:43
decisions.reason: Jesus says that the righteous will shine like the sun in their Father's kingdom (Matthew 13:43), in words that recall this verse.

decisions.choice: those who have insight (L); those who are wise (B); the wise leaders (R); the vault [of heaven] (L), the sky (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Those who have insight" keeps the wording of 11:33 and 35 at each level. "Vault" follows Genesis 1:6 at Literal, with "of heaven" bracketed; Balanced and Readable say "sky". Every level opens with a quotation mark, since this verse starts a new paragraph in the Hebrew within the messenger's speech.

decisions.choice: "la voûte [céleste]" (L), "le ciel" (B, R)
decisions.reason: "La voûte" is the term sheet's word for the raqia, as Genesis 1:6; Literal brackets the adjective that says which vault is meant, as the English brackets "of heaven".

source.text: וְאַתָּ֣ה דָֽנִיֵּ֗אל סְתֹ֧ם הַדְּבָרִ֛ים וַחֲתֹ֥ם הַסֵּ֖פֶר עַד־עֵ֣ת קֵ֑ץ יְשֹׁטְט֥וּ רַבִּ֖ים וְתִרְבֶּ֥ה הַדָּֽעַת׃

records.literal_gloss: And you, Daniel, keep secret the words and seal up the book until [the] time of [the] end; many will rove about, and will increase the knowledge.

en.L: "But you, Daniel, keep the words secret and seal up the book until the time of the end. Many will run to and fro, and knowledge will increase."
en.B: "But you, Daniel, keep these words secret and seal up the book until the time of the end. Many will search here and there, and knowledge will increase."
en.R: "But you, Daniel, keep this message secret. Seal up the book until the time of the end. Many people will go here and there trying to understand, and knowledge will grow."

fr.L: Mais toi, Daniel, tiens secrètes les paroles et scelle le livre jusqu’au temps de la fin. Beaucoup courront çà et là, et la connaissance augmentera. »
fr.B: Mais toi, Daniel, garde ces paroles secrètes et scelle le livre jusqu’au temps de la fin. Beaucoup chercheront de tous côtés, et la connaissance augmentera. »
fr.R: Mais toi, Daniel, garde ce message secret. Scelle le livre jusqu’au temps de la fin. Beaucoup de gens iront de tous côtés pour essayer de comprendre, et la connaissance grandira. »

decisions.choice: keep the words secret and seal the book: close and preserve it for its time
decisions.reason: As in 8:26. The book is shut and sealed so that it is kept unchanged until the time comes for it to be understood (verse 9). Revelation 22:10, by contrast, tells John not to seal his book, "for the time is near".

decisions.choice: many will run to and fro, and knowledge will increase
alternatives: many will roam about, and evil will increase
decisions.reason: The verb means to roam about. Amos 8:12 says that people "will run to and fro to seek the word of the LORD, but will not find it". Here it is usually read as many searching the book, until at the end knowledge grows. Some ancient translations read "evil" in place of "knowledge" (a small difference in Hebrew letters), giving "and evil will increase".

decisions.choice: search here and there (B); go here and there trying to understand (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "run to and fro"; Balanced and Readable give the usual sense (m2). The messenger's speech, which began at 10:20, ends here.

source.text: וְרָאִ֨יתִי֙ אֲנִ֣י דָנִיֵּ֔אל וְהִנֵּ֛ה שְׁנַ֥יִם אֲחֵרִ֖ים עֹמְדִ֑ים אֶחָ֥ד הֵ֨נָּה֙ לִשְׂפַ֣ת הַיְאֹ֔ר וְאֶחָ֥ד הֵ֖נָּה לִשְׂפַ֥ת הַיְאֹֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And I saw, I, Daniel, and look, two others standing, one here on [the] bank of the river and one here on [the] bank of the river.

en.L: Then I, Daniel, looked, and look, two others were standing, one on this bank of the river and one on that bank of the river.
en.B: Then I, Daniel, looked, and there before me stood two others, one on this bank of the river and the other on the opposite bank.
en.R: Then I, Daniel, looked and saw two other heavenly beings. One was standing on one side of the river, and the other on the other side.

fr.L: Et moi, Daniel, je regardai, et voici, deux autres se tenaient [là], l’un sur la rive du fleuve, de ce côté-ci, et l’autre sur la rive du fleuve, de ce côté-là.
fr.B: Alors moi, Daniel, je regardai, et voici que deux autres se tenaient là, l’un sur une rive du fleuve, l’autre sur la rive opposée.
fr.R: Alors moi, Daniel, j’ai regardé et j’ai vu deux autres êtres célestes. L’un se tenait d’un côté du fleuve, et l’autre de l’autre côté.

decisions.choice: the river: the Tigris of 10:4
decisions.reason: The word here is the one usually used for the Nile, but in this vision it is the river by which Daniel stood, the Tigris (10:4).

decisions.choice: two others: two more heavenly beings, as witnesses
decisions.reason: Two witnesses were needed to confirm a matter (Deuteronomy 19:15). The two stand on either bank as the man in linen swears an oath (verse 7).

decisions.choice: heavenly beings (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says who the "others" are.

source.text: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר לָאִישׁ֙ לְב֣וּשׁ הַבַּדִּ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר מִמַּ֖עַל לְמֵימֵ֣י הַיְאֹ֑ר עַד־מָתַ֖י קֵ֥ץ הַפְּלָאֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: And one said to the man clothed in linen, who [was] above the waters of the river: Until when [is the] end of the wonders?

en.L: And [someone] said to the man clothed in linen, who was over the waters of the river, "Until when [is] the end of these wonders?"
en.B: One of them asked the man dressed in linen, who stood above the waters of the river, "How long will it be until these astonishing things come to an end?"
en.R: One of them spoke to the man dressed in linen clothes, who was standing above the water of the river. He asked, "How long will it be until these amazing things are over?"

fr.L: Et [l’un] dit à l’homme vêtu de lin, qui était au-dessus des eaux du fleuve : « Jusqu’à quand [sera] la fin de ces merveilles ? »
fr.B: L’un d’eux demanda à l’homme vêtu de lin, qui se tenait au-dessus des eaux du fleuve : « Combien de temps faudra-t-il avant que ces choses extraordinaires prennent fin ? »
fr.R: L’un d’eux a parlé à l’homme habillé de vêtements de lin, qui se tenait au-dessus de l’eau du fleuve. Il lui a demandé : « Combien de temps faudra-t-il pour que ces choses étonnantes soient finies ? »

decisions.choice: the man clothed in linen: the figure of 10:5
decisions.reason: The heavenly figure Daniel saw at the start of the vision (10:5-6) now stands above the river.

decisions.choice: these wonders: the astonishing events foretold
decisions.reason: The word means extraordinary things, here the terrible events of chapter 11 and the end of 12:1-3 (compare 8:24; 11:36).

source.text: וָאֶשְׁמַ֞ע אֶת־הָאִ֣ישׁ׀לְב֣וּשׁ הַבַּדִּ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר מִמַּעַל֮ לְמֵימֵ֣י הַיְאֹר֒ וַיָּ֨רֶם יְמִינ֤וֹ וּשְׂמֹאלוֹ֙ אֶל־הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם וַיִּשָּׁבַ֖ע בְּחֵ֣י הָעוֹלָ֑ם כִּי֩ לְמוֹעֵ֨ד מֽוֹעֲדִ֜ים וָחֵ֗צִי וּכְכַלּ֛וֹת נַפֵּ֥ץ יַד־עַם־קֹ֖דֶשׁ תִּכְלֶ֥ינָה כָל־אֵֽלֶּה׃

records.literal_gloss: And I heard the man clothed in linen, who [was] above the waters of the river, and he raised his right [hand] and his left [hand] to the heavens, and swore by the one who lives forever that [it will be] for a time, times and a half; and when the shattering of [the] power of [the] holy people is finished, all these [things] will be completed.

en.L: And I heard the man clothed in linen, who was over the waters of the river; he raised his right hand and his left hand toward the heavens and swore by the one who lives forever that it would be for a time, times and half [a time]; and when the shattering of the power of the holy people comes to an end, all these things will be completed.
en.B: I heard the man dressed in linen, who was standing above the waters of the river, raise his right hand and his left hand toward heaven and swear by the one who lives forever: "It will be for a time, two times and half a time. Once the power of the holy people has been completely broken, all these things will be fulfilled."
en.R: The man dressed in linen, who was standing above the river, raised both his hands toward heaven. I heard him make a promise in the name of God, who lives forever. He said, "It will be three and a half periods of time. When the power of God's holy people has been completely broken, all these things will happen."

fr.L: Et j’entendis l’homme vêtu de lin, qui était au-dessus des eaux du fleuve ; il leva sa main droite et sa main gauche vers les cieux, et il jura par celui qui vit éternellement que [ce serait] pour un temps, des temps et la moitié [d’un temps] ; et quand l’écrasement de la force du peuple saint serait achevé, toutes ces choses s’accompliraient.
fr.B: J’entendis l’homme vêtu de lin, qui se tenait au-dessus des eaux du fleuve, lever la main droite et la main gauche vers le ciel et jurer par celui qui vit éternellement : « Ce sera pour un temps, deux temps et la moitié d’un temps. Quand la force du peuple saint aura été complètement brisée, toutes ces choses s’accompliront. »
fr.R: L’homme habillé de lin, qui se tenait au-dessus du fleuve, a levé les deux mains vers le ciel. Je l’ai entendu faire un serment au nom de Dieu, qui vit pour toujours. Il a dit : « Cela durera trois périodes et demie. Quand la force du peuple saint de Dieu aura été complètement brisée, toutes ces choses arriveront. »

decisions.choice: he raised both hands to heaven and swore: a solemn oath
decisions.reason: A person raised a hand to heaven to swear (Genesis 14:22; Deuteronomy 32:40). Raising both hands makes the oath doubly solemn. Revelation 10:5-6 describes a mighty angel standing on sea and land, raising his right hand to heaven and swearing by the one who lives forever.

decisions.choice: a time, times and a half: as in 7:25
decisions.reason: The same period as in 7:25, usually taken as three and a half years, half of seven, a time of suffering cut short. See the note there.

decisions.choice: when the shattering of the power of the holy people comes to an end: a hard phrase
alternatives: when the power of the one who shatters the holy people comes to an end
decisions.reason: The Hebrew may mean that the end comes when the power of God's people has been completely broken (their weakness is the sign of the end), or, with a change of letters, "when the power of the one who shatters the holy people comes to an end". The first is the Hebrew as it stands.

decisions.choice: the one who lives forever: God
decisions.reason: The oath is sworn by God, the ever-living (4:31; Deuteronomy 32:40).

decisions.choice: three and a half periods of time; God, who lives forever (R)
decisions.reason: Readable adds up the period as in 7:25, without saying how long a "time" is (compare 4:13), and names God. Balanced and Readable set the oath in quotation marks; Literal reports it as the Hebrew does.

decisions.choice: "un temps, des temps et la moitié [d'un temps]" (L), "un temps, deux temps et la moitié d'un temps" (B), "trois périodes et demie" (R), as 7:25
alternatives: "un temps, des temps et un demi-temps"
decisions.reason: As the term sheet sets for 7:25 and 12:7: Balanced reads the plural as two, and Readable gives the sum, as the English Readable "three and a half periods of time".

source.text: וַאֲנִ֥י שָׁמַ֖עְתִּי וְלֹ֣א אָבִ֑ין וָאֹ֣מְרָ֔ה אֲדֹנִ֕י מָ֥ה אַחֲרִ֖ית אֵֽלֶּה׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And I heard, but not I understood; and I said: My lord, what [will be the] outcome of these [things]?

en.L: And I heard, but I did not understand. So I said, "My lord, what will the end of these things be?"
en.B: I heard, but I did not understand. So I said, "My lord, how will all this turn out?"
en.R: I heard what he said, but I did not understand. So I asked, "Sir, how will all this end?"

fr.L: Et j’entendis, mais je ne compris pas ; et je dis : « Mon seigneur, quelle [sera] l’issue de ces choses ? »
fr.B: J’entendis, mais je ne compris pas. Je dis donc : « Mon seigneur, comment tout cela finira-t-il ? »
fr.R: J’ai entendu ce qu’il disait, mais je n’ai pas compris. Alors j’ai demandé : « Mon seigneur, comment tout cela va-t-il finir ? »

decisions.choice: the outcome: the last part, what comes at the end
decisions.reason: The word means the end or latter part of something. Daniel asks what the final result of these things will be.

decisions.choice: Sir (R)
decisions.reason: As in 10:16-17, "my lord" is a polite address to the heavenly messenger, and Readable says "Sir".

source.text: וַיֹּ֖אמֶר לֵ֣ךְ דָּנִיֵּ֑אל כִּֽי־סְתֻמִ֧ים וַחֲתֻמִ֛ים הַדְּבָרִ֖ים עַד־עֵ֥ת קֵֽץ׃

records.literal_gloss: And he said: Go, Daniel, for kept secret and sealed up [are] the words until [the] time of [the] end.

en.L: And he said, "Go, Daniel, for the words are kept secret and sealed until the time of the end.
en.B: He said, "Go your way, Daniel, for the words are kept secret and sealed until the time of the end.
en.R: He said, "Go on your way, Daniel. These words are to be kept secret and sealed until the time of the end.

fr.L: Et il dit : « Va, Daniel, car les paroles sont tenues secrètes et scellées jusqu’au temps de la fin.
fr.B: Il répondit : « Va ton chemin, Daniel, car ces paroles sont tenues secrètes et scellées jusqu’au temps de la fin.
fr.R: Il a répondu : « Continue ton chemin, Daniel. Ces paroles doivent rester secrètes et scellées jusqu’au temps de la fin.

decisions.choice: go: go your way, do not ask further
decisions.reason: The command gently closes the conversation: Daniel is not to know more now. It comes again in verse 13.

decisions.choice: kept secret and sealed until the time of the end
decisions.reason: The words of verse 4 again. The meaning will be clear only when the time comes.

source.text: יִ֠תְבָּֽרֲרוּ וְיִֽתְלַבְּנ֤וּ וְיִצָּֽרְפוּ֙ רַבִּ֔ים וְהִרְשִׁ֣יעוּ רְשָׁעִ֔ים וְלֹ֥א יָבִ֖ינוּ כָּל־רְשָׁעִ֑ים וְהַמַּשְׂכִּלִ֖ים יָבִֽינוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: Many will purify themselves and make themselves white and be refined; but will act wickedly [the] wicked, and not will understand any [of the] wicked, but those having insight will understand.

en.L: Many will purify themselves, will make themselves white, and will be refined; and the wicked will act wickedly; and none of the wicked will understand, but those who have insight will understand.
en.B: Many will be purified, made white and refined, but the wicked will go on doing evil. Not one of the wicked will understand, but those who are wise will.
en.R: Many people will be made pure and clean, like metal in a fire. But the wicked will keep on doing evil. None of the wicked will understand, but the wise leaders will understand.

fr.L: Beaucoup se purifieront, se blanchiront et seront affinés ; et les méchants agiront méchamment, et aucun des méchants ne comprendra, mais ceux qui ont du discernement comprendront.
fr.B: Beaucoup seront purifiés, blanchis et affinés, mais les méchants continueront à faire le mal. Aucun des méchants ne comprendra, mais les sages comprendront.
fr.R: Beaucoup de gens seront purifiés et rendus propres, comme le métal dans le feu. Mais les méchants continueront à faire le mal. Aucun des méchants ne comprendra, mais les sages qui guident le peuple comprendront.

decisions.choice: purified, made white and refined: as in 11:35
decisions.reason: The three verbs of 11:35, in a different order. The time of suffering refines the faithful.

decisions.choice: those who have insight will understand: the wise will grasp the meaning when the time comes
decisions.reason: The book sealed until the end (verses 4, 9) will be understood by the wise of that time. Compare Revelation 22:11.

decisions.choice: those who have insight (L); those who are wise (B); the wise leaders (R)
decisions.reason: As in 11:33 and 12:3.

source.text: וּמֵעֵת֙ הוּסַ֣ר הַתָּמִ֔יד וְלָתֵ֖ת שִׁקּ֣וּץ שֹׁמֵ֑ם יָמִ֕ים אֶ֖לֶף מָאתַ֥יִם וְתִשְׁעִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And from [the] time the regular [offering] is removed and to set up [the] abomination making desolate, [there will be] days one thousand two hundred and ninety.

en.L: And from the time that the regular [offering] is taken away and the abomination that makes desolate is set up, [there will be] 1,290 days.
en.B: From the time that the regular offering is abolished and the abomination that brings ruin is set up, there will be 1,290 days.
en.R: From the time the daily sacrifices are stopped and the horrible thing that brings ruin is set up, there will be 1,290 days.

fr.L: Et depuis le temps où le [sacrifice] continuel sera enlevé et où l’abomination de la désolation sera dressée, [il y aura] 1 290 jours.
fr.B: Depuis le moment où le sacrifice régulier sera supprimé et où l’abomination qui apporte la ruine sera dressée, il y aura 1 290 jours.
fr.R: Depuis le moment où les sacrifices de chaque jour seront arrêtés et où la chose horrible qui détruit sera installée, il y aura 1 290 jours.

decisions.choice: 1,290 days: about three and a half years
decisions.reason: 1,290 days is a little more than three and a half years of 360 days (1,260 days, Revelation 11:3; 12:6), with a month added. Verse 12 adds a further 45 days. Why the numbers differ is not explained: they may be later additions that extend an earlier figure as the time passed, or count to different events, or mark stages of the end. Compare the 2,300 evenings and mornings of 8:14.

decisions.choice: the abomination that makes desolate: 9:27; 11:31; Matthew 24:15 and Mark 13:14
decisions.reason: The phrase of 11:31, taken up by Jesus in Matthew 24:15 and Mark 13:14. In the usual reading it is the pagan altar set up in the temple in 167 BC (1 Maccabees 1:54).

decisions.choice: the abomination that makes desolate (L); the abomination that brings ruin (B); the horrible thing that brings ruin (R)
decisions.reason: The wording follows the table for Daniel and 11:31, and that of Matthew 24:15 at Balanced and Readable (and Mark 13:14 at Balanced).

decisions.choice: the regular [offering] (L); the regular offering (B); the daily sacrifices (R)
decisions.reason: As in 8:11 and 11:31. The number is written in figures at every level, as the style guide does for numbers above ninety-nine.

source.text: אַשְׁרֵ֥י הַֽמְחַכֶּ֖ה וְיַגִּ֑יעַ לְיָמִ֕ים אֶ֕לֶף שְׁלֹ֥שׁ מֵא֖וֹת שְׁלֹשִׁ֥ים וַחֲמִשָּֽׁה׃

records.literal_gloss: How blessed [is] the one who waits and reaches to days one thousand three hundred thirty and five.

en.L: How blessed [is] the one who waits and reaches the 1,335 days!
en.B: How blessed is the one who waits and reaches the end of the 1,335 days!
en.R: Life is truly good for the person who keeps waiting until the 1,335 days are over!

fr.L: Heureux celui qui attend et qui atteint les 1 335 jours !
fr.B: Heureux celui qui attend et qui parvient au terme des 1 335 jours !
fr.R: Quel bonheur pour celui qui continuera d’attendre jusqu’à la fin des 1 335 jours !

decisions.choice: how blessed: how happy, how well off
decisions.reason: The word is the one that opens Psalm 1. It describes the true good of the person who keeps faith and waits.

decisions.choice: the one who waits and reaches: who holds on to the end
decisions.reason: The verb means to wait in hope (Isaiah 30:18; Habakkuk 2:3). Blessing comes to the one who endures to the end of the time set (compare Matthew 24:13).

decisions.choice: How blessed (L, B); Life is truly good for (R)
decisions.reason: The wording of Psalm 1:1 at each level. "The one who" and "the person who" already include men and women, so no gender span is needed.

decisions.choice: "Heureux celui qui" (L, B), "Quel bonheur pour celui qui" (R)
decisions.reason: "Heureux" is the usual French for this exclamation, as in the Psalms and the Beatitudes; Readable makes it a plain exclamation, as the English Readable does.

source.text: וְאַתָּ֖ה לֵ֣ךְ לַקֵּ֑ץ וְתָנ֛וּחַ וְתַעֲמֹ֥ד לְגֹרָלְךָ֖ לְקֵ֥ץ הַיָּמִֽין׃

records.literal_gloss: And you, go to the end; and you will rest and will stand for your lot at [the] end of the days.

en.L: But you, go [your way] to the end; and you will rest, and you will stand for your allotted portion at the end of the days."
en.B: As for you, go your way until the end. You will rest, and at the end of the days you will rise to receive your inheritance."
en.R: But you, Daniel, go on your way until the end. You will die and rest. But at the end of time you will rise from death to receive your reward."

fr.L: Mais toi, va jusqu’à la fin ; et tu te reposeras, et tu te tiendras [debout] pour ta part à la fin des jours. »
fr.B: Quant à toi, va ton chemin jusqu’à la fin. Tu te reposeras, et à la fin des jours tu te lèveras pour recevoir ta part d’héritage. »
fr.R: Mais toi, Daniel, continue ton chemin jusqu’à la fin. Tu mourras et tu te reposeras. Mais à la fin des temps, tu te relèveras de la mort pour recevoir ta récompense. »

decisions.choice: go to the end: live out your life to its end
decisions.reason: Daniel is to go on to the end of his life, or until the end the vision speaks of, and leave the outcome with God.

decisions.choice: you will rest and will stand for your lot: Daniel will die and be raised
decisions.reason: "Rest" is the rest of death (Isaiah 57:2; Job 3:13, 17). "Stand" here means rise up, as the dead "awake" in verse 2, to receive his "lot", the share allotted to him, as each tribe received its lot in the land (Joshua 14:2). The book ends with the promise of resurrection to Daniel himself.

decisions.choice: you will stand for your allotted portion (L); you will rise to receive your inheritance (B); you will rise from death to receive your reward (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "stand" and "lot"; Balanced and Readable say what they mean here (m2). Readable says "die" for "rest" and names Daniel. The messenger's words, which began in verse 9, close the book.
